mainTopic: Checking a doubtful duck, רבי יהודה's rule about the ורידין, and whether exactly half of a סימן counts as a majority
overview: This amud opens by finishing a practical problem. רבא has a duck with a bloody neck, and he needs to know whether its קנה was already cut or its ושט has a hole. The גמרא rejects checking it after שחיטה and also rejects checking it before. רב יוסף, רבא's son, solves the problem: check the קנה, slaughter through the קנה alone, then turn the ושט inside out and check it. From this the גמרא learns that in a bird, 'one סימן' can be either one. Next, רב חסדא says רבי יהודה requires cutting the ורידין only in a bird, so that the blood drains. Several sources seem to make the veins part of the שחיטה itself. Each one is reread to mean puncturing them during the שחיטה, while the blood is still warm. An elder adds that the veins may even be punctured with a thorn, and a ברייתא supports רב חסדא. Finally, רב and רב כהנא argue whether exactly half of a סימן counts as a majority, and the גמרא tests רב's view with proofs that continue onto the next amud.

steps.title: Slaughter first, then check? That will not work
steps.stepSummary: The idea of slaughtering the duck first and checking it afterward is rejected. The cut might land right on the hole.
steps.simpleTranslation: Should we slaughter it and then check it? But maybe he will cut right where the hole is!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests one way to settle the doubt about the duck and then knocks it down right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you slaughter first, the knife may pass through the exact spot of a hole in the ושט. Then the hole is gone inside the cut, and you can never know whether the bird was a טריפה before the שחיטה.
steps.confusionAlert: This text picks up in the middle of a story. The 'it' is a duck whose neck was bloody, and the question is whether its ושט had a hole (טריפה) or its קנה was already cut.

phrases.english: Let us slaughter it and then examine it?
phrases.notes: 'It' is the duck with the bloody neck from just before this point in the daf.

phrases.english: Perhaps he will slaughter right at the place of the hole!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's doubt about the duck from just before this point in the daf.
steps.kashyaTarget: The option of slaughtering before checking
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Slaughtering could cut through the hole and wipe out the evidence.

steps.title: Check first, then slaughter? That will not work either
steps.stepSummary: The idea of checking the duck before slaughtering is rejected because of רבה's rule that the ושט can only be checked from the inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: Should we check it and then slaughter it? But רבה said: the gullet cannot be checked from the outside, only from the inside!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the opposite order, checking first, and rejects it using a rule from רבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the bird is alive you can only see the outside of the ושט. רבה taught that a hole in the ושט can only be properly seen from the inside. So checking first does not settle the doubt.

phrases.english: Let us examine it and then slaughter it?
But Rabba said:
The gullet has no examination from the outside
but only from the inside!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting 'slaughter first', the גמרא tries 'check first' and rejects that too.
steps.kashyaTarget: The option of checking before slaughtering
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבה's rule says a check of the ושט from the outside is not reliable.

steps.title: רב יוסף's solution: cut the windpipe, then check the gullet
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף suggests checking the קנה, slaughtering through the קנה alone, and then turning the ושט inside out to check it.
steps.simpleTranslation: His son רב יוסף said to him: Check the windpipe, then slaughter through the windpipe and make it kosher that way. Then turn the gullet inside out and check it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא's son offers a way out that avoids both problems.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קנה can be checked from the outside, so you can first see that it was not already cut. A bird only needs one סימן cut, so cutting the קנה alone makes a kosher שחיטה and leaves the ושט untouched. After that, the ושט can be turned inside out and checked properly, which also satisfies רבה's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: let us turn it over (inside out)

phrases.english: Rav Yosef, his son, said to him:
phrases.notes: 'His son' means רבא's son, who was the one asking about the duck.

phrases.english: Let us examine the windpipe,
and slaughter the windpipe and make it kosher,
and then turn the gullet inside out and examine it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Solves the problem that blocked both earlier options.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical procedure that sidesteps both objections
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed that either order of checking and slaughtering would fail.
steps.terutzMaskana: Cut only the קנה, which is enough for a bird, and leave the ושט whole so it can be checked from the inside.

steps.title: רבא praises his son
steps.stepSummary: רבא says his son Yosef is as wise in the laws of טריפות as רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: My son Yosef is as wise in the laws of טריפות as רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא approves of his son's solution with high praise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The praise shows that רבא accepts the solution in practice. This sets up the inference the גמרא draws next.

keyTerms.meaning: defects that make an animal or bird forbidden

phrases.english: Rava said: My son Yosef is wise
in the laws of tereifot like Rabbi Yoḥanan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא reacts to and accepts רב יוסף's solution.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יוסף's procedure is accepted as correct.

steps.title: So 'one סימן' can be either one
steps.stepSummary: From this story, the גמרא learns that the משנה's 'one סימן' for a bird can be either the ושט or the קנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We see that the 'one' the משנה mentions means either this one or that one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a lesson from the duck story about how to read the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף's plan only works if cutting the קנה alone is a kosher שחיטה for a bird. Since רבא accepted it, the משנה's 'one סימן' cannot be limited to the ושט. Either סימן is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: either this one or that one
one of the two organs cut in שחיטה (קנה or ושט)

steps.whatToRemember: For a bird, cutting just one סימן is enough, and it can be either the קנה or the ושט.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical rule for slaughtering birds: either סימן works.

phrases.english: Apparently, the 'one' that it says
phrases.notes: This refers to the משנה's rule that in a bird, cutting one סימן is enough.

phrases.english: means either this one or that one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general rule from the accepted solution.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In a bird, cutting either the קנה or the ושט is a valid שחיטה.

steps.title: Quoting רבי יהודה in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to a new topic: רבי יהודה's view in the משנה that the שחיטה is not done until the ורידין are cut.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: Not until he cuts the veins.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה to begin a new discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה text here is short. In the full משנה, רבי יהודה says the cut must also reach the ורידין, the neck veins. The next steps ask what his reason is.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: Until he cuts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה requires cutting the ורידין.

steps.title: רב חסדא: Only in birds, because of the blood
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא limits רבי יהודה's rule to birds, which are roasted whole. An animal is cut into pieces, so the blood comes out anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: רבי יהודה said this only about a bird, because people roast it whole. But an animal is cut up limb by limb, so cutting the veins is not needed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא explains the reason for רבי יהודה's rule, and that reason limits the rule to birds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב חסדא, cutting the ורידין is about getting the blood out. A whole roasted bird keeps its blood unless the veins are cut. An animal is cut into limbs, so its blood drains out anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: he cuts it up limb by limb

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אֶלָּא בְּעוֹף,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said this only about a bird,
since one roasts it whole, all at once,
but an animal,
since one cuts it up limb by limb
– it is not needed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: לֹא אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אֶלָּא בְּעוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains and limits רבי יהודה's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cutting the ורידין is required only for birds, so that the blood will drain.

steps.title: Is it really about blood? The משנה calls it שחיטה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא. The משנה's wording 'until he slaughters the veins' sounds like cutting the veins is part of the שחיטה itself, not just a way to drain blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are you saying רבי יהודה's reason is because of the blood? But we learned in the משנה: רבי יהודה says, until he slaughters the veins!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב חסדא's explanation using the exact wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word שישחוט means 'slaughter'. That suggests cutting the veins is part of making the שחיטה valid. If the reason were only blood, the משנה would not describe it with the language of שחיטה.

phrases.english: Is that to say that the reason of Rabbi Yehuda
is because of the blood?
But didn't we learn: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Until he slaughters the veins.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּטַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה מִשּׁוּם דָּם הוּא? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason רב חסדא gave in the previous step.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's claim that רבי יהודה's reason is draining blood
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה uses the word for slaughtering, which suggests the veins are part of the שחיטה, not just about blood.

steps.title: Rereading the משנה: puncture the veins during the slaughter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading 'until he slaughters the veins' as 'until he punctures the veins at the time of שחיטה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Say that the משנה means 'until he punctures the veins.' Then why does it say 'until he slaughters'? It means: until he punctures them at the time of the שחיטה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב חסדא. It says the משנה's word 'slaughter' only tells us when to cut the veins, not that cutting them is part of the שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge in step 8 was that 'slaughter the veins' sounds like the veins are part of the שחיטה. The answer keeps רב חסדא's view that the veins are cut only to let the blood out. The word 'slaughter' is read as a time marker: do it while the שחיטה is happening.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Say': the גמרא suggests a different way to read the words
The two large blood vessels (jugular veins) in the neck
To puncture, to make a hole in
At the time of the slaughter, while it is happening

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree that the veins are cut during the שחיטה. The real question is why. If cutting them is part of the שחיטה itself, it would apply to animals too. If it is only to drain the blood, רב חסדא can limit it to birds, which are roasted whole.

phrases.english: Say: 'until he punctures the veins,'
and what does 'until he slaughters' mean?
Until he punctures them at the time of slaughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 8
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Until he slaughters the veins' means the veins are part of the שחיטה
steps.terutzMaskana: It means puncturing the veins during the שחיטה, so the blood can drain

steps.title: A ברייתא says the veins are 'through slaughter'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to say רבי יהודה counts the veins as part of the שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'The veins are through slaughter.' These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to challenge רב חסדא again. The ברייתא seems to link the veins to the שחיטה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'the veins through slaughter' sound like the veins must be cut as part of the act of שחיטה. If so, the rule would apply to animals too, which goes against רב חסדא's limit to birds.

keyTerms.meaning: Through slaughter, as part of the שחיטה
A teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה

phrases.english: Come and hear: 'The veins are through slaughter,'
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to רב חסדא after the answer in step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's view that the veins are cut only to drain blood
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's wording seems to make the veins part of the שחיטה itself

steps.title: Rereading the ברייתא: puncture them during the slaughter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the ברייתא as 'the veins must be punctured at the time of שחיטה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Say that the ברייתא means: the veins must be punctured at the time of the שחיטה. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with the same move as before. It reads 'through slaughter' as 'at the time of slaughter.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is added to רבי יהודה's view. The ברייתא is read like the משנה was in step 9: it is about timing, not about the veins being part of the שחיטה.

phrases.english: Say: 'The veins must be punctured'
at the time of slaughter; these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 10
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'The veins through slaughter' means they are part of the שחיטה
steps.terutzMaskana: It means they must be punctured during the שחיטה

steps.title: The חכמים' argument shows רבי יהודה linked the veins to slaughter
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records the חכמים arguing with רבי יהודה in a way that suggests he holds the veins are part of the שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: The חכמים said to רבי יהודה: Since the veins were mentioned only to drain the blood from them, what difference does it make to me whether it is done through slaughter or not through slaughter? We learn from this that רבי יהודה holds the veins are cut through slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא against רב חסדא. This time the proof comes from how the חכמים answered רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים argue that the veins only matter for draining blood, so it should not matter whether they are cut 'through slaughter' or not. That argument only makes sense if רבי יהודה holds that they must be cut as part of the שחיטה, which goes against רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: To drain the blood out of them
'What is it to me': what difference does it make?

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע: אָמְרוּ לוֹ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: Come and hear: They said to Rabbi Yehuda,
'Since the veins were not mentioned'
except to drain the blood from them,
what difference is it to me if it is through slaughter,
or not through slaughter?'
This implies that Rabbi Yehuda holds it is through slaughter.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: אָמְרוּ לוֹ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A stronger challenge after step 11's answer
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's view that the veins are cut only to drain blood
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חכמים' reply only makes sense if רבי יהודה holds that cutting the veins is part of the שחיטה

steps.title: The חכמים were really arguing about timing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the חכמים were asking why the veins must be punctured during the שחיטה rather than afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what they were saying: What difference does it make to me whether he punctures them at the time of the שחיטה or punctures them not at the time of the שחיטה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rereads the חכמים' words. Their argument was about when to puncture the veins, not about whether the veins are part of the שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read this way, everyone agrees the veins are only for draining blood. The only disagreement is whether you must do it during the שחיטה, or whether it is fine to do it later.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is what they are saying': the גמרא explains what the speakers really meant

phrases.english: This is what they were saying:
What difference is it to me whether he punctures them at the time of slaughter,

phrases.aramaic: מָה לִי לְנַקְּבָן שֶׁלֹּא בִּשְׁעַת שְׁחִיטָה?
phrases.english: or punctures them not at the time of slaughter?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 12
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חכמים were arguing about whether the veins are part of the שחיטה
steps.terutzMaskana: The חכמים were arguing only about when the veins must be punctured

steps.title: Why רבי יהודה wants it done during the slaughter: warm blood flows
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה holds that the veins must be punctured during the שחיטה because warm blood flows out, while cold blood does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה holds: at the time of the שחיטה the blood comes out, because it is warm. Not at the time of the שחיטה, the blood does not come out, because it has cooled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer by giving רבי יהודה's reason for doing it during the שחיטה. The reason is all about getting the blood out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fully supports רב חסדא. רבי יהודה's demand for timing is about blood: warm blood drains and cold blood stays in. So the rule is about removing blood, which fits limiting it to birds that are roasted whole.
steps.whatToRemember: Every source is read to mean that רבי יהודה wants the veins punctured during the שחיטה only so the warm blood drains out. Cutting the veins is not part of the שחיטה itself. That keeps רב חסדא's view standing: the rule is for birds, which are roasted whole.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the timing rule comes from the goal of removing blood. That is the basis for רב חסדא's limit to birds.

phrases.aramaic: וְהוּא סָבַר: בִּשְׁעַת שְׁחִיטָה אָתֵי דָּם דְּחָיֵים,
phrases.english: And he holds: at the time of slaughter the blood comes out, because it is warm;

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא בִּשְׁעַת שְׁחִיטָה לָא אָתֵי דָּם דְּקָרִיר.
phrases.english: not at the time of slaughter, the blood does not come out, because it has cooled.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהוּא סָבַר: בִּשְׁעַת שְׁחִיטָה אָתֵי דָּם דְּחָיֵים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes step 13's answer by giving רבי יהודה's reason
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the reasoning behind the timing
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Cutting the veins during the שחיטה must be part of the שחיטה itself
steps.terutzMaskana: It must be done during the שחיטה only because warm blood drains and cold blood does not

steps.title: Do pausing or pressing ruin the cutting of the veins?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks: according to רבי יהודה, if someone paused or pressed down while cutting the veins, is the שחיטה ruined?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה asked: according to רבי יהודה, who requires the veins to be cut, what if he paused or pressed while cutting them? What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה asks a real question. Do the rules that can ruin a שחיטה, like pausing or pressing, also apply when cutting the veins?
steps.deeperAnalysis: שהיה and דרסה ruin a שחיטה when they happen while cutting the סימנים. The question is whether the veins are treated like the סימנים. If they are part of the שחיטה, these problems would ruin it. If they are only a separate step to drain the blood, they would not.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised a question (a real doubt about the law)
Pausing in the middle of the שחיטה, which makes it invalid
Pressing the knife down instead of moving it back and forth, which makes the שחיטה invalid

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya asked:
The veins, according to Rabbi Yehuda,
if he paused while cutting them, or pressed while cutting them, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the conclusion that the veins are punctured to let warm blood out. It asks whether this means the veins follow the rules of שחיטה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Do the rules of שהיה and דרסה apply to cutting the veins according to רבי יהודה?

steps.title: The veins can even be punctured with a thorn
steps.stepSummary: An elder answers in the name of רבי אלעזר, or in another version in the name of רבי יוחנן, that the veins may be punctured with a thorn and it is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain elder said to him: this is what רבי אלעזר said. Others say a certain elder said to רבי אלעזר that this is what רבי יוחנן said: he may puncture the veins with a thorn, and it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: An elder answers רבי ירמיה's question. You can even poke a hole in the veins with a thorn, and the animal stays kosher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a thorn is good enough, the veins clearly do not need a real שחיטה. So the rules that ruin a שחיטה, like pausing and pressing, do not apply to them. The גמרא also records two versions of who said this.

keyTerms.meaning: A certain elder, an unnamed old scholar

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה, cutting the veins is only for draining blood. It is not part of the שחיטה itself, so pausing or pressing there does not matter.

phrases.english: A certain elder said to him:
This is what Rabbi Elazar said,
and some say:

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָהוּא סָבָא לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר,
phrases.english: A certain elder said to Rabbi Elazar,
This is what Rabbi Yochanan said:
He punctures them with a thorn, and they are valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers רבי ירמיה's question from step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The veins may be punctured even with a thorn. So they are not part of the שחיטה, and pausing or pressing does not ruin anything.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב חסדא: the veins are needed only in a bird
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports רב חסדא. Cutting half of each סימן is invalid in a bird and in an animal, and רבי יהודה requires the gullet and the veins only in a bird.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא supports רב חסדא. If someone cut half of each of the two סימנים in a bird, it is invalid, and of course in an animal. רבי יהודה says: in a bird, it is not valid until he cuts the gullet and the veins.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up רב חסדא. רבי יהודה's requirement to cut the veins is said only about a bird.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה says "in a bird" when he requires the veins. That shows his rule is limited to birds and does not apply to animals, which is just what רב חסדא said. The first part of the ברייתא also teaches that two half-cut סימנים do not add up to a valid שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: In line with him, supporting his view
Halves of the סימנים, the two pipes cut in שחיטה
Needless to say, it is even more obvious

phrases.english: It was taught in a ברייתא in line with Rav Chisda:
phrases.notes: רב חסדא said that רבי יהודה requires cutting the veins only in a bird, not in an animal.

phrases.aramaic: שָׁחַט שְׁנֵי חֲצָאֵי סִימָנִין בְּעוֹף – פָּסוּל,
phrases.english: If he cut two halves of the simanim in a bird, it is invalid,
phrases.notes: He means half of each pipe. Two halves do not add up to one whole סימן.

phrases.english: and needless to say in an animal.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
In a bird, it is not valid until he cuts
the gullet and the veins.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רב חסדא's earlier view about the veins and brings support for it from a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's view that רבי יהודה requires the veins only in a bird
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where רבי יהודה says "in a bird" when requiring the gullet and the veins

steps.title: Is exactly half of a סימן like a majority?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about half of one סימן in a bird and brings a dispute. רב says exactly half counts as a majority. רב כהנא says it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: half of one סימן in a bird, and so on. It was stated: רב said that exactly half counts like a majority. רב כהנא said that exactly half does not count like a majority.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a new line in the משנה and brings an argument between אמוראים. The argument is about a סימן cut exactly half-way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says cutting half of one סימן in a bird is invalid, because a bird needs a רוב of one סימן. רב holds that exact half counts as a majority. רב כהנא holds it does not. This sets up the discussion of how רב fits with the משנה.
steps.confusionAlert: The משנה says half of one סימן in a bird is invalid, which seems to go against רב. Steps 21-22 raise this problem and explain how רב fits with the משנה.
steps.whyThisMatters: Whether exact half counts as a majority matters for every case in שחיטה that needs a רוב of a סימן.

phrases.english: Half of one in a bird, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה: cutting half of one סימן in a bird is not valid.

phrases.english: It was stated:

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָמַר: מֶחֱצָה עַל מֶחֱצָה כְּרוֹב,
phrases.english: Rav said: exactly half and half is like a majority,

phrases.aramaic: רַב כָּהֲנָא אָמַר: מֶחֱצָה עַל מֶחֱצָה אֵינוֹ כְּרוֹב.
phrases.english: Rav Kahana said: exactly half and half is not like a majority.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of the veins and opens a new topic from the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: a סימן cut exactly half-way counts as a majority. רב כהנא: it does not count as a majority.

steps.title: The reasoning behind רב and רב כהנא
steps.stepSummary: רב says exactly half counts as a majority, because the rule is 'do not leave a majority uncut.' רב כהנא says it does not, because the rule is 'cut a majority.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: exactly half is like a majority, because this is what ה׳ told משה: 'Do not leave over the majority.' רב כהנא said: exactly half is not like a majority, because this is what ה׳ told משה: 'Slaughter the majority.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the reasoning behind the dispute it just introduced. Each side explains how he understands the instruction given to משה about how much to cut.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree on the case: half cut, half uncut. They differ on how the rule is worded. If the rule is 'don't leave a majority uncut,' exactly half passes, since the uncut part is not a majority. If the rule is 'cut a majority,' exactly half fails, since the cut part is not a majority either.

keyTerms.meaning: Exactly half and half: half cut, half not cut
Like a majority, treated as if most was cut
Do not leave over the majority (רב's wording)

steps.whatToRemember: רב: 'don't leave most uncut,' so by Torah law exactly half is כשר. רב כהנא: 'cut most,' so exactly half is פסול.
steps.confusionAlert: Neither one disagrees about the facts. Exactly half was cut in both views. The only question is how the rule is phrased, which decides whether half is enough.
steps.whyThisMatters: This dispute sets up the rest of the sugya. Every proof that follows is testing which wording is correct.

phrases.english: Rav said:
half against half is like a majority,
this is what the Merciful One said to Moshe:
phrases.notes: This isn't a פסוק. He's describing the oral teaching משה received about how שחיטה is done.

phrases.english: "Do not leave over the majority."
Rav Kahana said:
half against half is not like a majority,
this is what the Merciful One said to Moshe:
"Slaughter the majority."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning for each side of the dispute introduced in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: exactly half cut is valid, since the rule is not to leave a majority uncut. רב כהנא: exactly half is invalid, since the rule is to cut a majority.

steps.title: A memory aid for the coming proofs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a list of key words to help remember the four proofs it is about to bring about this dispute.
steps.simpleTranslation: (Memory aid: Half, קטינא, windpipe, damage.)
steps.whatsHappening: This line is a setup. The גמרא is giving a short list of words to help us remember the order of the proofs that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word points to one coming proof. 'Half' is the משנה about half a סימן. 'קטינא' is רב קטינא's ברייתא. 'Windpipe' and 'damage' are later proofs. It is not a legal statement, just a way to remember.

keyTerms.meaning: Here it means a memory aid (not the organs cut in שחיטה)

steps.confusionAlert: The word סימן here does not mean the windpipe or gullet that are cut in שחיטה. It means a memory list.

phrases.english: (Memory aid: Half, Ketina,
phrases.notes: These are code words for the proofs that come next, in order.

phrases.english: windpipe, damage.)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Prepares the list of proofs that will test the dispute from step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling. It is a memory aid for the four proofs that follow.

steps.title: Challenge to רב from the משנה about half a סימן
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says cutting half of one סימן in a bird is פסול. If exactly half counts as a majority, as רב says, why is it פסול?
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: half of one סימן in a bird, or one and a half in an animal, makes the שחיטה invalid. If you say exactly half is like a majority, why is it invalid? He did cut a majority!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב's view using our משנה, which calls cutting half a סימן invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bird needs only one סימן cut. If half equals a majority, cutting half of that one סימן should be enough. Yet the משנה rules it פסול, which seems to fit רב כהנא and contradict רב.

keyTerms.meaning: A bird, which needs only one סימן cut
An animal, which needs both סימנים cut

phrases.english: We learned in the משנה:
half of one סימן in a bird,
and one and a half in an animal —
his slaughter is invalid.

phrases.aramaic: אִי אָמְרַתְּ מֶחֱצָה עַל מֶחֱצָה כְּרוֹב,
phrases.english: If you say half against half is like a majority,
why is it invalid?
He has done a majority!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ מֶחֱצָה עַל מֶחֱצָה כְּרוֹב, אַמַּאי פָּסוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the first proof on the memory list ('half'), aimed against רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's view that exactly half counts as a majority
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה rules half a סימן in a bird invalid. Under רב, half should equal a majority and the שחיטה should be valid.

steps.title: The משנה is only a rabbinic safeguard
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that by Torah law half is enough, as רב says. The Rabbis made it פסול so that a person won't end up cutting less than half.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is invalid by rabbinic law, because perhaps he will not end up cutting even half.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב. The משנה's ruling is a rabbinic extra safeguard, not the Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nobody can cut exactly half with full accuracy. If people relied on cutting half, they might sometimes cut a little less. So the Rabbis required more than half, while by Torah law exactly half would still count.

keyTerms.meaning: By rabbinic law, not Torah law

phrases.english: By rabbinic law,
lest he come not to cut even half.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּרַבָּנַן, דִּלְמָא לָא אָתֵי לְמֶעְבַּד פַּלְגָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21 in defense of רב.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the levels of law: the Torah allows half, and the Rabbis added a stricter rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's ruling that half is פסול was taken as Torah law, which would disprove רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: Torah law accepts exactly half, as רב says. The משנה's invalidation is a rabbinic precaution against cutting less than half.

steps.title: רב קטינא's proof from an object split into equal halves
steps.stepSummary: רב קטינא brings a ברייתא: if an impure item is split into two seemingly equal parts, both stay impure, because it is impossible to split it exactly. This is brought as a challenge to רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב קטינא said, come and hear: if he split it in two and they are equal, both are impure, because it is impossible to be exact.
steps.whatsHappening: רב קטינא brings a new source, the second item on the memory list, to test the dispute. It is brought as a challenge to רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא deals with an impure clay vessel that becomes pure when broken. The larger piece stays impure. When the two halves look equal, both stay impure, because we cannot be sure neither one is bigger. The ברייתא gives the reason 'it is impossible to be exact,' and this is brought to challenge רב's claim that an exact half counts as a majority.

keyTerms.meaning: It is impossible to be perfectly exact

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not about שחיטה at all. It is about breaking an impure vessel. The גמרא borrows it only because it also deals with an exact half.

phrases.english: Rav Ketina said, come and hear:
if he split it in two and they are equal —
phrases.notes: 'It' is an impure clay vessel. Breaking it makes it pure, but the bigger piece stays impure.

phrases.english: both are impure,
because it is impossible to be exact.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first challenge was answered, a second source (the 'קטינא' item on the memory list) is brought against רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's view that exactly half counts as a majority
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא about an object split into equal halves is brought to show that an exact half is not simply treated as a majority, which challenges רב.

steps.title: If an exact split would make both halves pure, how can half count as a majority?
steps.stepSummary: From the ברייתא's reason, the גמרא infers that an exact split would make both halves טהור. That goes against רב, because each half would then count as a majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies that if it were possible to split it exactly, both halves would be pure. But why pure? Look at this half: it is a majority. Look at that half: it is also a majority!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now spells out how the ברייתא from step 23 is a challenge to רב. It reads the ברייתא's reason and draws out what it implies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says both halves stay impure only because an exact split cannot be made. So if it could be made, both would be טהור. But if exactly half counts as a majority, as רב says, each half should be treated as 'most' of the vessel and stay impure.

keyTerms.meaning: To measure or divide with perfect precision

phrases.english: This implies: if it were possible to divide exactly, they would be pure.
But why should they be pure?
Go here, there is a majority,
go there, there is a majority!
phrases.notes: If half counts as most, as רב says, then each half counts as most of the vessel.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא אֶפְשָׁר לְצַמְצֵם – טְהוֹרִין, אַמַּאי טְהוֹרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge that רב קטינא opened in step 23 by drawing the inference from the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's view that exactly half counts as a majority
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא implies an exact half-split would make both halves טהור. If half equals a majority, each half should count as a majority of the vessel and stay impure. The ruling of טהור shows half is not a majority.

steps.title: One vessel cannot have two majorities
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that in the vessel case, half cannot be treated as a majority because both halves would then be majorities at once.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: There cannot be two majorities in one vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא defends רב. He explains why the vessel case is different from cutting a סימן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the vessel, calling one half a majority means calling the other half a majority too, and that makes no sense. So there, half does not count as a majority. When cutting a סימן there is no competing half, so exactly half can count as a majority, as רב says.
steps.whatToRemember: Half can count as a majority only when there is no other half competing to be the majority. That is why the vessel case does not disprove רב.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
There cannot be two majorities in one vessel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: תְּרֵי רוּבֵּי בְּחַד מָנָא לֵיכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 24 and defends רב.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: a split vessel would create two competing majorities, but a cut סימן does not.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The vessel case shows that half is never treated as a majority.
steps.terutzMaskana: Half cannot be a majority when the other half would also be one. Where there is no rival half, as in cutting a סימן, רב's rule still works.

steps.title: A new proof begins: cutting half the windpipe and pausing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting another source, about someone who cut half the windpipe and then paused, as a new challenge to רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If he cut half the windpipe and paused in the middle of it...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next challenge to רב. It starts quoting a ברייתא, and the case continues on the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is about someone who cut exactly half the windpipe and then stopped. The ruling has not been given yet. The גמרא will use it to test whether half counts as a majority.

keyTerms.meaning: The windpipe (trachea), one of the two סימנים
He paused or delayed in the middle of the שחיטה

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If he cut half the windpipe,
and paused in it

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: שָׁחַט חֲצִי גַרְגֶּרֶת, וְשָׁהָה בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the vessel challenge is answered, the גמרא moves to the next proof from its list in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's view that exactly half counts as a majority
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This is only the setup. The ruling about cutting exactly half and pausing will be used to test רב's view.
